name: v5.1.78
body:
### Changed

- Hephaestus on GPT-6.2 models sends one prompt instead of two: the GPT-6.2 core stands alone there, so the Hephaestus role is no longer appended after it. Other models keep the role, and switching models in a session drops or restores it. On a real request the system prompt goes from 9,211 to 4,300 tokens (`o200k_base`). The refusal-is-final rule is now stated once inside the model-core frame for every agent that carries it instead of at the end of the role, so it survives without the role and is never doubled by a model core that states it. ([#14219](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14219), part of [#14186](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14186)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))
- **No behaviour change: tests now pin which ended sessions a fuzzy handoff compares.** A fuzzy handoff still compares only the ended sessions that could change its answer. Tests now prove the cut-off, and that a session left out never appears in the list an ambiguous handoff asks you to pick from. ([#13190](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13190), follows #13141) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- Thread tools in one process share a single endpoint enumeration per agent dir, instead of one per session, so a session that a delivery just started reuses a listing taken within the last 5 s. ([#13236](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13236), part of [#12989](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12989)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- **Every recovery hint in the thread tools now gives the eval-cell form beside the tool name (`thread_list (tool.thread_list() in an eval cell)`), the convention the thread tool descriptions already follow.** A model that follows a hint no longer hits the "run it in an eval cell" redirect first. ([#13240](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13240)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- A thread tool call on an account with other devices reads the account's session list once instead of up to three times: overlapping reads share one listing round, and a round that ended under 2 s ago answers the next read (a create, open or session command lists again). The account list waits on every device, 0.5-2 s on a loaded fleet. ([#13453](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13453)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- `thread_list` rows carry a `state` (`running`, `idle`, `inactive` or `archived`) and the thread's `model` when known, instead of a per-thread live/alive flag; whether a device is reachable is on `devices` only. Archived threads are hidden unless a `state` filter asks for them (`omo thread list --state`), and a thread closed on this device stays listed as inactive instead of disappearing. `status` remains for now, derived from the state. ([#13469](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13469), fixes [#13403](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13403)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- **`omo remote` takes a device by the name its table prints.** The session verbs (`open`, `send`, `model`, `interrupt`, `close`) accept a device's id, its name (compared as thread names are) or a unique id prefix, through the same resolver `thread_create` uses, and their output names the device by its id. A name two online devices share is refused with `ambiguous_target`, listing each candidate; a name only an offline device has is `device_offline`; a device nothing matches is `not_found`. ([#13499](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13499), [#13432](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13432)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- The thread control port's `setThinkingLevel` no longer takes a `scope` argument that nothing read: both the local and the relay control always change only the addressed session's level (engine scope `turn`) since #13494. No behavior change. ([#13500](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13500)) ([#13506](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13506)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- Creating a thread on another of your devices (`thread_create` with `device`, `omo remote open`) is faster. The create used to make four round trips over the relay: it looked up the device's engine endpoint, opened the session, attached to it, and named it. Now it makes two. The endpoint is looked up once per device, nothing attaches to the new session, and the name goes straight to it. ([#13889](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13889), part of [#13404](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13404)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- An omo session now reaches this device's device service over one connection instead of two: the thread tools' session commands share the connection their account reads already use, and closing the remote client ends it. ([#13944](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13944)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))

### Fixed

- `omo remote send` that waits on a turn now settles inside a bound: `--timeout <seconds>` (1..600, default 120) answers a typed `{kind:"timeout", waited_ms, ...}` JSON value instead of hanging when the turn never settles; a session that ends before settling answers `{kind:"session_ended", end}` as one JSON value under `--json` (both were a silent hang or stderr-only), and the queued notice rides that same JSON value instead of being dropped (#13425). ([#14213](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14213)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))
- `thread_create` reopens a closed thread on another device again. It failed with `EISDIR`: the account listing names a session's working folder, never its session file, and that folder was sent to the other device as the file to open (a row with no path sent its working folder too). The reopen now opens the file the close was told by that device, or else asks the device which file carries the thread's id; a device that cannot say answers a typed refusal naming it (`unsupported` for an engine without the lookup, `not_found`, or `ambiguous_target`). A thread this device closed no longer lists as `live` while the listing catches up, and a reopen answers `ok` only once the reopened session can be reached, so the next tool call no longer answers `not_resumable`. ([#14179](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14179), fixes [#14170](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14170)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))
- `thread_send` to a thread on another device that is not running answers at once instead of waiting about 60 seconds for `unsupported` (`daemon_unavailable`). The device holding it is asked first, whether or not this device can wake it there: a thread it holds no session file for is `not_found` (as the refused reopen says), one it runs is delivered to (also when it was reopened elsewhere since this device last listed it, under whatever key it runs under now), and one it only has on disk is woken when this device can wake it there, else `not_resumable`, naming the reopen as the next step. A device without the wake capability counts as unable to wake. ([#14179](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14179), fixes [#14184](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14184)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))
- `thread_send`, `thread_read` and `thread_create` aimed at another device no longer wait past what an eval tool call allows: the command waits, wakes, creates and attaches of one call now share one 50 s budget, and a `thread_read` wait on another device leaves the read after it enough time to return the transcript. A message the relay accepted for the other device but whose answer was lost is reported as the new `delivered_unconfirmed` (it may have run: read the thread before sending again). ([#14185](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14185)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))
- `thread_create` (and `omo remote open`) on another device now opens the thread only on that device's own engine (the primary engine endpoint its device service names), never on the first endpoint listed. Before this, a thread could land on an owner shard or on another registered agent dir's older engine, which then refused every cross-device `thread_send` as unsupported (`method_unclassified`). When the device names no primary, because its own engine is not listed, the create now fails `host_unavailable` with reason `no_primary_endpoint` before anything opens, even if only one other endpoint is listed. The next action says to start or restart omo on that device, and to update the device service on both devices if that does not help (a device service older than 0.1.11 cannot name a primary; behind such a local service a device's lone endpoint is still used). ([#14200](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14200), fixes [#14195](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14195)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))
- `thread_send` no longer answers `not_found` for a thread that `thread_list` shows live while the other device's service is restarting for an update, or when that device missed one account listing round. It now answers a retryable `host_unavailable`, so the sender can try again instead of treating the thread as gone. ([#14174](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14174), fixes #14172; this entry was missing from the #14196 train's notes) ([#14203](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14203)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))
- A newer gateway store schema of an extension is no longer reported as the gateway's own schema with that extension's migration counts. ([#14221](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14221)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))
- When a thread created on another device cannot be named because this device is signed out, the warning now names this device's sign-in instead of telling you to update omo on that device. ([#14221](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14221)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))
- `thread_create` with an alias held by a thread on another device no longer opens a copy of that thread's session file on a third device as if it were the holder. ([#14221](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14221)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))
- The remote wake's engine minimum now also holds back a compiled omo or dev build when a caller sets a stricter minimum, and an omo prerelease no longer counts as its release. ([#14221](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14221)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))
- A reply's route and the listing it takes are decided from one read of this device's id, and a late endpoint listing no longer replaces a terminal's kind that another session's newer listing recorded. ([#14221](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14221)) ([#14225](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14225))
- On Windows, a memory sync and a memory write starting together on a new device no longer fail with a held `memory-write` lock. Creating the memory repository there takes longer than the 5 s lock wait, so the second caller timed out. Callers in one process now wait for the one creation already running. ([#14223](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14223), fixes [#14188](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14188))
- Memory sync's root-change check no longer reports "unchanged" when the newest retired trust pin is corrupt, truncated or belongs to another account; it reports the check as skipped (`PIN_UNREADABLE`) instead of comparing against an older pin. A missing pin still falls back to the next older one. ([#14218](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14218))
- Input sent over a session's RPC socket (`prompt`, `steer` or `follow_up`) now counts as typed input for the thread tools. A run it starts or joins never claims the input as a delivery it received: when the client reused the id of a real delivery that this session never received, `thread_send` was refused `invalid_arguments` (`guard: "unknown_cause"`) or continued a chain the session was not part of. Such a send now starts a new causal chain, and a run the gateway started from a bound thread keeps that thread's chain (#12317). ([#12318](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12318)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- `thread_create` that opens an existing thread and passes the alias that thread already holds (`{thread: X, alias: X}`, or the thread's id with its own alias) now opens it and keeps the alias, instead of failing `alias_taken` with the thread itself named as the holder. An alias held by another thread is still `alias_taken`. ([#12732](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12732)) ([#14175](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14175)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- When another device refuses a `thread_send` or `thread_handoff` because the chain went past that device user's thread chain limit (`threads.chainCountLimit`), the tool now answers `chain_count_limit`, naming the device and the setting, instead of `unsupported` with advice to update omo on that device. A queued delivery to a session there that is not running maps a chain-limit refusal from that device's gateway store to the same code, with the chain count and the limit, and the receiving consumer now passes on the store's own refusal reason (for example `sender_not_allowed`) instead of the coarse code. ([#12766](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12766)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- **A send to another device whose state read gets no answer can be retried right away.** When the `get_state` read that a steer to another device starts with ends without an answer, `thread_send` now reports `host_unavailable` (nothing was sent there, retry is safe) instead of `idempotency_uncertain`, and a retry under the same `idempotency_key` reads the target again instead of replaying that failure; a send that fails before its record leaves this device keeps no receipt. ([#12947](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/12947), fixes [#12925](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12925), part of [#12879](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12879)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- **A delivery message without a valid id no longer inherits the previous sender's reply allowance.** A `session_control_delivery` whose `delivery_id` is not a string is malformed: after a final answer it starts a new group with nobody approved, and while work is running it joins the work without adding a sender or changing the hop - it no longer passes as a turn the engine started (which kept the earlier group's allowance). The same-account bound of the reply allowance is stated where the rule runs (`component.ts` `noteInput` and the thread `AGENTS.md`), not only in the release notes. ([#13134](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13134)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- **A thread named by its alias after a late sign-in is still answered when the rename fails, and says why.** When the account is gone by the alias claim and the rename that names the new thread by the alias fails with an untyped error, `thread_create` now answers `ok` with the created thread and `local_name_unavailable: "host_unavailable"`, instead of an error that did not name the thread. The error's message comes back as `local_name_unavailable_reason`, cut to 300 characters with an ellipsis, so a failure can be traced without a whole host reply filling the result. ([#13185](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13185), follows #13179; folds #13283 and #13284) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- A thread tool call no longer waits forever behind an endpoint enumeration (`host status --all`) that never answers: after 30 s the next call starts a fresh one and the stuck answer is dropped. ([#13231](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13231), fixes [#13009](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13009)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- **Text from another device prints escaped in the thread tools' output.** A thread title, project path or refusal reason that another device sends is shown with its control, format and line-separator characters escaped (`\u202e`, `\^[`, ...) wherever `thread_list`, `thread_read`, `thread_create` and the control tools print it, including the candidates of an ambiguous name; nothing is deleted, and addressing a thread by its exact title still finds it. ([#13305](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13305), [#13304](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13304)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- Thread tools: a command for a session that ended on another device since it was listed now fails with `not_resumable` ("the thread is not running on device X") instead of `unsupported` with advice to update omo on that device. ([#13439](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13439)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- Thread tools (`thread_list`, `thread_read`, `thread_send`, `thread_create`, ...) and `omo thread` no longer run `host status --all` on every call. They read the endpoint registry on disk instead, so a local `thread_list` that took about 9 s on a host with 50 endpoints answers in well under a second. ([#13452](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13452)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- Listing a thread endpoint that stopped answering reads its leftover session claims asynchronously, so an endpoint with many stale claims no longer blocks the engine's event loop while `thread_list` runs (fixes #13551, folded from #13573). ([#13452](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13452)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- A reply to a sender named by its device no longer goes through the relay when this device's own id cannot be read; the send is refused `host_unavailable` with the reason, and nothing is sent. ([#13483](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13483), part of [#13037](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13037)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- A session that another device holds but does not run is reached through a probe only while this device's service can carry the wake; with the wake off, the answer stays `not_found` instead of an attach refusal. ([#13483](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13483)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- A wake whose connection drops after the request was written is reported uncertain, not refused, so it is never retried as if nothing ran. The list of local API codes that refuse before sending now lives once in `device-service-core` and is shared with the thread tools. ([#13483](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13483)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- When another device's service refuses a wake with free-form text, that text is no longer shown; the reason reads `unrecognised`, as it already did for the receiving consumer's refusals. ([#13483](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13483), part of [#13277](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13277)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- `thread_list` drops the cached rows of a device the account no longer lists, so `thread_create` and `thread_send` answer `not_found` for that device's thread instead of addressing it; an offline device keeps its rows, and with no account device list the filter is a no-op. ([#13539](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13539)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- Listing a thread endpoint that stopped answering reads its leftover claims and the session files they name asynchronously and one at a time, so a host that died holding many sessions neither blocks the engine's event loop nor runs it out of file descriptors while `thread_list` runs. Endpoints are still listed together, so the files open at once are bounded by the number of endpoints, not by the number of stale claims. ([#13581](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13581), fixes #13579 and #13584) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- Cold wake: a message from another device now wakes sessions on installs of the compiled omo binary (the one-line installer) too. The wake checked the engine version in a form only npm installs report, so it stayed off on compiled installs (#13672). ([#13673](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13673)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- Cold wake: a message that arrives while the woken session is still being restored now runs once the restore settles. It no longer waits for you to open the session (#13708). ([#13709](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13709)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- `thread_read` with `wait_ms` on a thread on another device no longer settles early while the session retries after a provider error: the retry's `auto_retry_start` / `auto_retry_end` records now count as the run still going, so the wait ends on the retried run's turn (#13871). ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- An agent whose omo build is older than the one that last upgraded this machine's gateway store no longer gets an opaque `internal_error` from `thread_send` and the other thread tools (or `omo thread send`). The store is still refused, so nothing is read or written at a schema the build does not know, and the failure is now `gateway_schema_too_new`: it names the store's schema and the build's schema, and tells you to update omo with the exact command (`omo update`), then restart the session. ([#13941](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13941), fixes [#13927](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13927)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- Thread tools: a call toward another device that this device cannot send because its own relay sign-in lapsed (`sign_in_required`, `signed_out`) now fails with `host_unavailable` asking to sign in on this device, instead of `unsupported` with advice to update omo on the other device. ([#14015](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14015)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- `thread_read` with a small `max_bytes` now returns the newest messages that fit, ending at the latest reply, on this device and on another one. Before, it filled the budget from the oldest message of the 60-message window, so a 1.5 KB read of a short thread returned only its preamble. `next_cursor` from such a read pages the older messages of the window. ([#14176](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14176)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- When the host refuses to close a thread, the `thread_close` refusal (`unsupported`) now names the engine's reason in its message, for example `refused to close it (work_pending: an admitted delivery not yet written)`. Before, the message named only the reason code, so a caller could not tell a running turn, a bash command and an undelivered message apart. The engine side of the same bug, where an interrupted run left a delivery that kept every close refused, is fixed in code-yeongyu/senpi#6971. ([#14178](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14178), fixes [#14169](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14169)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- Remote sessions: a session host unit written by an older omo (`KeepAlive` / `Restart=always`, naming an older `~/.omo/binary-runtime/<version>/omo`) is brought to the launched runtime's run-once shape and program on the first launch of a newer runtime, keeping its own agent directory and `PATH`, never re-enabling a disabled unit and never blocking the launch; a refused ensure no longer respawns every 30 s. `omo daemon run` now says why the engine refused, on which socket and which host holds it. ([#14194](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14194), fixes [#14191](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14191))
- Codex edition recon agents: `explorer` and `librarian` bundled TOMLs default to `gpt-6-luna` at `low` on the `fast` service tier instead of the flagship `gpt-6-astra`, matching the cheap recon routing every other edition's model tables already pin (#8616). Untouched installs step down on the next sync through the model-receipt mechanism; a hand-set model or effort keeps surviving the move. The other ten roles keep Astra at their current efforts. ([#14192](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14192), fixes [#14189](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14189))
- Memory sync: when the newest retired trust pin cannot be read, the root-change check is reported as skipped instead of silently comparing against an older pin; the recovery-phrase terminal reader zeroes its buffer when released. ([#14105](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14105), fixes [#14098](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14098))
- Memory sync: a join, enable or passkey recovery that already pinned the account is no longer reported as failed when the follow-up root-change check cannot read the local retired pins. The check is reported as skipped instead of passing silently: `omo sync enable` prints it with the error code, the desktop's enable result carries an optional `rootCheck: { kind: "skipped", reason }` beside `rootChanged`, the in-app warning goes to the memory component's log rather than the terminal, and recovery emits `sync.trust.root_check_skipped`. ([#13641](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13641), fixes [#12382](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/12382)) ([#14097](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14097))
- Memory sync: creating a recovery phrase now checks the sync service's own answer on whether it accepts recovery-phrase keys, read fresh through the signed-in session for every creation. Before this the host never wired that check, so a recovery phrase could not be created even where the service accepts one. A refused, absent, unreadable or signed-out answer still refuses before any words are shown or anything is written. ([#13646](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13646), fixes [#13631](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13631)) ([#14097](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14097))
- Memory sync works again after a recovery phrase is set up. The sync engine's requests (batches, objects, uploads, sync state and the event stream), the device-list read and the account reads now declare the client contract version and the recovery-phrase capability, as the account and pairing requests already did. Before this, the service refused every one of them with "client update required" for an account with a recovery phrase, so no device synced (#13691). ([#13693](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13693)) ([#14097](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14097))
- Memory sync no longer stops for good when its first start fails. A start that fails (for example another omo process holding the account's credential lock past the 15 s wait) or gets stuck is retried on the same backoff as a waiting start, 15 s doubling to five minutes. A stuck start is named in the log, and the first successful start logs "memory sync started", so a log shows whether sync is running (#13701). ([#13706](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13706)) ([#14097](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14097))
- Memory sync: a device that has turned sync on and joined the account now receives the account's memory without writing anything first. Its memory repository is created through the same first-write path a memory write uses, only for a joined device with sync on; a device that has not joined, a device with sync off and every read still create nothing. ([#14096](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14096), fixes [#14094](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/14094)) ([#14097](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14097))

### Added

- `thread_archive { thread, archived? }` archives or unarchives a thread on any device through the engine's session flag. ([#13469](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13469), part of [#13407](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13407)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- **Scripts can create, interrupt, close, rename and re-model threads through the thread SDK.** `createThreadSdk(...)` from `runtime/thread-sdk/sdk.js` now has `create`, `interrupt`, `close`, `rename` and `set_model`. They take the same arguments as `thread_create`, `thread_interrupt`, `thread_close`, `thread_rename` and `thread_set_model`, run the same code, and answer the same data on this device or another device of the account. A script acts as itself, not as a session, so `self` answers `caller_context_missing` and a thread it creates records no creator session. ([#13413](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/13413)) ([#13495](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13495)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- `thread_list` rows of a held thread carry the engine's `activity` (`idle`, `running`, `awaiting_approval`, `queued` or `errored`), `error_code` with `errored`, and `turn_id` when the engine reports them (senpi#6688). `state` folds them: `queued` and `awaiting_approval` are `running`, `errored` is `idle`; inactive and archived rows carry none. ([#13504](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13504)) ([#14196](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14196))
- Memory sync can be turned off on one device. `omo sync disable` turns it off for the device it runs on: that device stops sending and receiving memory, memory already on it stays, and the account's other devices keep syncing. `omo sync enable` turns it on again without a new approval. An OmO session already running on that device stops syncing when its sync next reports a change, or at its next start, and a process that turns sync on again starts the engines it had stopped right away. For the desktop, the engine answers `omo.memory.sync.disable` with `{ kind: "off" }` or a typed problem, and lists `"disable"` in `omo.memory.sync.features`; turning off from the desktop app needs an app release that carries the matching request. ([#14121](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14121))
- The memory sync status can say how many memories changed while this device was offline: `status.sync.appliedWhileOffline` is the number of memories the catch-up updated after the device was away (OmO was closed, or sync could not reach the service), `0` when nothing changed, and absent when the latest changes arrived while it was online. ([#14121](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14121))
- `omo sync enable` and `omo sync recover` can use a recovery phrase on the terminal itself: words appear only on the controlling terminal, never in output or logs, and the flow refuses under an agent harness, CI or without a terminal. Creating a phrase still needs the client flag, and the CLI asks the service whether it accepts phrase keys before each creation. ([#13337](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13337)) ([#14097](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14097))

name: @openviking/react 0.2.0
body:
## en-US

### Minor Changes

- 609baba: Let FileBrowser hosts load experience metrics and override individual experience dashboard sections.

- 704bec6: Add optional FileBrowser props for hosts to save and restore expanded folders independently of the selected resource.

  Hosts can also persist explicit collapses across mounts when home alias resolution is temporarily unavailable.

### Patch Changes

- 7a15a83: Make the AgentConnect full-instruction copy button more prominent and clarify its labels. Allow the instruction header and copy button to wrap in narrow containers regardless of component stylesheet import order. Unify rounded, theme-aware instruction cards, code blocks and tables, and keep a single table border even when only a header is present.

- 9dd10ec: Consolidate compile help under one Console entry and document the model and schedule fields in `--args`.

- 8a52885: Support session auto-creation, memory policies, context token budgets, and retained message counts in Console. Send structured message parts, creation timestamps, and batch JSON. Session write commands accept boolean or JSON object telemetry options and display the server's telemetry summary with a label in the current Console language.

- 4c11e48: Console can restore read-only command history after a refresh in the same browser tab when the host provides a scoped `commandHistoryKey`.

- 9f03f45: Add Compile create before Compile in the Console quick-start actions and fill in the command syntax for both. Clarify the compile configuration and directory parameters in the built-in help, and keep parameter descriptions readable in narrow popovers.

- 989e6c7: Show the error message directly when a command fails. If the API error message is blank, show its error code.

- 9f03f45: Keep Console command history in local storage for each configured library and user scope. The history menu and arrow-key recall restore the same submitted commands after a reload, including asynchronous resource imports.

- 61a0546: Keep resource URIs with spaces clickable in Console result URI fields and quoted URI arguments. In plain text, Markdown code, and free-text command arguments, link each URI token separately.

- 8a52885: Keep the Deleted badge on confirmed file deletions in the history and comparison picker. The file must exist in the first parent. Older servers can confirm deletion through snapshot diff. Compare with an earlier version to see the removed content. Missing snapshot content for a tracked file appears as a read error.

- 8a52885: Disable dates outside the selected search range and reject reversed ranges entered by hand.

- 442638c: Restore `compile create` as a separate Console entry before `compile`, split their guidance, and align creation parameters with the latest product copy.

- 94b18d3: Switch retrieval modes at the top of the FileBrowser results area, including when the result count is zero. Switching modes retains the query and compatible filters.

- 8a52885: Show the resource name on the preview tab immediately when opening a Wiki compilation or conflict dashboard.

- c16c4cc: VikingBot now uses dedicated controls for Wiki and scheduled update questions, supports submitting the current session for memory extraction, and presents rename and delete in a menu on each history entry.

  Console can also show a Bot activation screen and open the conversation when a host confirms the current library's Bot is ready.

- 704bec6: Return focus to the VikingBot session history button when a session dialog closes and focus would otherwise fall back to the page. The tooltip stays hidden after mouse dismissal and remains available on hover and keyboard focus.

- 8a52885: Keep Wiki conflict highlights visible while any part of a highlighted block remains. Open the selected conflict in the editor, close conflict tooltips when scrolling or leaving the editor, and show a success notice after saving a Wiki file.

## zh-CN

### 功能更新

- 609baba: 支持 FileBrowser 宿主加载经验应用指标，并按区块覆盖经验看板的展示。

- 704bec6: FileBrowser 增加可选属性，支持宿主独立保存和恢复目录展开状态与选中资源。

  主目录别名暂时无法解析时，宿主也可通过完整快照跨挂载保存手动折叠记录。

### 修复与改进

- 7a15a83: 突出 AgentConnect 完整指令复制按钮并明确其文案，支持说明标题栏和复制按钮在窄容器内换行，不受组件样式引入顺序影响。统一说明卡片、代码块和表格的圆角及主题背景，仅有表头的表格也保持单层边框。

- 9dd10ec: 将编译指引集中到终端的一个入口，并补充 `--args` 的模型与定时字段说明。

- 8a52885: Console 支持自动创建会话、配置记忆策略、设置上下文 Token 预算和保留消息数，并支持发送结构化消息片段、指定创建时间和批量写入 JSON 消息。会话写入命令接受布尔值或 JSON 对象类型的遥测参数，并展示服务端返回的遥测摘要，标签随 Console 语言切换。

- 4c11e48: 宿主提供按身份范围隔离的 `commandHistoryKey` 后，Console 可在同一浏览器标签页刷新时恢复只读命令历史。

- 9f03f45: 在 Console 快速体验中将 compile create 放在 compile 前面，点击可填入对应的命令模板。补充终端帮助中的编译配置和目录参数说明，并避免窄浮窗将说明列挤得过窄。

- 989e6c7: 命令执行失败时，结果正文直接展示错误消息。接口返回的错误消息为空时，展示错误码。

- 9f03f45: 按配置的库和用户作用域在本地存储中保存 Console 命令历史。刷新后，历史菜单和方向键可回查同一份已提交的命令，包括异步资源导入命令。

- 61a0546: 终端结果的 URI 字段和带引号的 URI 参数会为含空格的资源路径保留完整链接。普通文本、Markdown 代码和自由文本参数按 URI 逐项生成链接。

- 8a52885: 确认文件删除的版本会在文件历史和对比下拉框中保留「已删除」标记。该路径在首父提交中必须是文件，旧版服务端也可以通过快照差异确认删除。与更早的版本对比可查看删除的内容。仍在快照中跟踪的文件如果缺失存储内容，则显示读取错误。

- 8a52885: 置灰会导致范围倒序的日期，并阻止手动输入倒序范围。

- 442638c: 恢复独立的 `compile create` 终端入口并放在 `compile` 前，拆分两条命令的指引，按最新产品文案补齐创建参数。

- 94b18d3: 文件浏览器在结果区顶部提供检索方式切换入口，检索到 0 条结果时也会显示条数并支持切换。切换时保留输入词和新模式支持的筛选。

name: v16.0.1
body:
## Critical fixes

- **Signing in to Codex works again on Windows while claude-mem runs** (#6332, thanks @ffe111, closes #6331). The private Codex home that claude-mem's app-server uses got its `auth.json` through a hard link to your real `~/.codex/auth.json`. Codex refuses to replace a credential file with more than one hard link (`persist_failed: atomic credential replacement does not support hard-linked files`), so `codex login` and token refresh failed for as long as that home existed. The private home now gets a symlink, which Codex follows. Only on Windows, and only when a symlink is not permitted (no Developer Mode or elevation), it gets a private copy instead. Any other error still fails loudly.
- **A probe answered with `<skip_summary/>` ends the quota cooldown** (#6324, thanks @vaibhav375, closes #6322). After a quota hit, the worker probes the provider and clears the cooldown once a probe stores a memory. A probe the provider answered with a valid `<skip_summary/>` stores nothing, so the cooldown never cleared and the worker re-probed every 5 minutes for as long as that session only skipped. A valid skip now releases the cooldown too, on both the store path and the early path before the memory session id is known. Observer-health success still needs a real store.

## Fixes

- **Search falls back to SQLite instead of failing when Chroma is slow** (#6327, thanks @REI-330, closes #6323). The MCP client gives a search 30 s, while each Chroma read waited up to 60 s, so a slow query was still running when the caller gave up and the SQLite/FTS5 fallback never ran. A search now shares one 20 s budget across its Chroma reads and falls back when it runs out, without restarting a healthy chroma-mcp.
- **Chroma rebuilds no longer hold a core for hours** (#6299, thanks @srieteja). A full backfill now pauses after each row for its write time times `CLAUDE_MEM_CHROMA_BACKFILL_PAUSE_RATIO` (default 1, 0 turns it off), and chroma-mcp starts under `nice` (`CLAUDE_MEM_CHROMA_PROCESS_NICE`, default 10) outside Windows. Live sync is unchanged.
- **Windows process cleanup reads taskkill correctly** (#6328, thanks @REI-330; #6307). A taskkill exit 255 is now judged by whether the named processes are still alive, not by its wording, so a localized message no longer throws during Chroma teardown, and a mixed message no longer reports success while a process still runs.
- **Observer turns stop leaking SQLite statements** (#6306). The statements that store an observer turn are cached instead of prepared on every turn, which could pile up until SQLite ran out of memory and rolled back the whole turn.
- **The login notice says when the observer has no Claude Code login it can use** (#6321, refs #6319). Instead of telling you to run `/login` when the terminal is signed in to another credential profile, the worker logs a warning with the reason and the notice names which login it read and suggests `claude setup-token`.
- **The legacy `claude-mem` shell alias is found and removed on install and update** (#6300, thanks @0xABCD01). `doctor` reports it, `status` warns when the worker runs outside the resolved plugin root, multiline aliases are left untouched with a warning, and nothing is changed if you cancel the reinstall.
- **`/api/health` publishes probe state only** (#6309, thanks @DeryFerd). It no longer shows the auth method, the Redis queue descriptor, absolute install paths or the last interaction to unauthenticated callers.
- **An unreadable My Work refresh status no longer breaks setup** (#6305). A damaged `refresh.json` reads as no run and gets replaced; the auto-updater still treats it as busy.
- **Local work stays paused when the machine runs out of file descriptors** (#6303). The setup check treats EMFILE/ENFILE as "setup still active" and logs one warning per episode.
- **Timeline file labels look the same on every platform** (#6301, thanks @POWDER-RANGER).
- **A press anywhere on a My Work focus card opens its area** (#6315). The same fix covers the List, Team and By agent rows.

## New

- **Devin cloud sessions and Devin Bots** (#6334). An organization can install `plugin/` as a Devin plugin and get hooks, MCP search and skills in every session.
- **My Work refresh on OpenCode** (#6330, thanks @REI-330). Opt in with `CLAUDE_MEM_WORK_VIEW_AGENT=opencode`; nothing changes otherwise.
- **PostgreSQL search finds terms inside CJK, kana and Hangul text** (#6329, thanks @REI-330, refs #3982).
- **My Work card titles name the task in 5 to 7 words** instead of copying the first sentence of the ask (#6317).
- **The image viewer darkens and blurs the page behind it** and casts a shadow (#6313).
- **The installer asks for your work email and a message in the terminal** before GUI setup (#6308).

## Tests and docs

- Grok Bot and Zed tests pass on Windows (#6311, #6312, thanks @Lupin133).
- Community sweep worktrees install with `bun install` (#6325).

name: supervision-0.32.0
body:
# v0.32.0: Zone counting, dwell time and semantic segmentation

## 📋 Summary

supervision now counts objects entering and leaving a zone, times how long each one stays, and loads semantic segmentation results.

- **`PolygonZone`** counts entries and exits per class and reports dwell time for every tracked object.
- **`Detections.from_semantic_segmentation`** turns a class map into one masked detection per class; Ultralytics and Inference results load too.
- **`KeyPointsDataset`** reads and writes YOLO pose datasets.
- **`box_weighted_box_fusion`** merges overlapping boxes from several models instead of throwing most of them away.
- **`VertexAnnotator`** and its siblings take a color palette and can color each joint by its index.

Most projects can upgrade as is, but the public `validate_*` helpers, `merge_inner_*` and `KeyPoints.confidence` are gone and a few edge cases changed, so check the Migration guide.

## ✨ Spotlights / highlights

### Zones that count entries, exits and dwell time

`sv.PolygonZone` now follows each `tracker_id` across frames. It counts objects entering and leaving (`in_count`, `out_count` and the per-class versions are named the same as on `sv.LineZone`), reports the current count per class, and measures how long each tracked object has been inside with `time_in_zone`. Pass a `timestamp` to `trigger` for seconds, or leave it out for frames. `occupancy_ratio` reports how much of the zone the detections cover, and `sv.PolygonZoneAnnotator` and `sv.LineZoneAnnotator` accept a `coord_transform` to draw at camera-mapped positions. (#2770, #1667, #2760)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/450b5c15-ae96-4990-93aa-28484b8c49cd

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

zone = sv.PolygonZone(polygon=np.array([[0, 0], [100, 0], [100, 100], [0, 100]]))

# A car drives in from the left, stays a while, then leaves on the right.
for frame, cx in enumerate([-10, 30, 50, 70, 90, 130]):
    car = sv.Detections(
        xyxy=np.array([[cx - 10, 40.0, cx + 10, 60.0]]),
        tracker_id=np.array([1]),
        class_id=np.array([0]),
    )
    zone.trigger(car, timestamp=frame * 0.5)
    if frame == 4:
        zone.time_in_zone(car)  # array([1.5]) seconds inside so far

zone.in_count, zone.out_count  # (1, 1)
zone.in_count_per_class  # {0: 1}
```

### Semantic segmentation maps load into `Detections`

`sv.Detections.from_semantic_segmentation` converts a class map, a base64 PNG or an integer array, into one detection per class with a mask of all its pixels and its class name. The background id `0` is dropped unless you pass `background_id=None`. `from_inference` now routes Roboflow Inference semantic results, such as RF-DETR semantic models, through it, and `from_ultralytics` loads Ultralytics `task="semantic"` results that used to come back empty. (#2898, #2915)

![A house photo next to its semantic segmentation result, one labelled mask per class](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/baf3ebe5-f964-4b0f-a19d-4acc6c8c40c3)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

class_map = np.zeros((6, 8), dtype=np.int64)
class_map[2:, :4] = 1  # road
class_map[:3, 5:] = 2  # sky

detections = sv.Detections.from_semantic_segmentation(
    class_map, class_map={1: "road", 2: "sky"}
)
detections.data["class_name"]  # array(['road', 'sky'], dtype='<U4')
detections.mask.shape  # (2, 6, 8)
```

### YOLO pose datasets as `sv.KeyPointsDataset`

Load, split, merge and write YOLO pose datasets. Images load lazily, the dataset supports indexing, and for labels with three values per point (x, y, visibility), the raw visibility stays under `data["keypoint_visibility"]`. (#2745)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

key_points = sv.KeyPoints(
    xy=np.array([[[20, 20], [50, 30], [40, 80]]], dtype=np.float32),
    class_id=np.array([0]),
)
dataset = sv.KeyPointsDataset(
    classes=["person"],
    images=["images/a.jpg"],
    annotations={"images/a.jpg": key_points},
    keypoint_count=3,
    value_dim=2,
)
dataset.as_yolo(
    images_directory_path="out/images",
    annotations_directory_path="out/labels",
    data_yaml_path="out/data.yaml",
)
restored = sv.KeyPointsDataset.from_yolo("out/images", "out/labels", "out/data.yaml")
```

### Weighted Box Fusion for ensembles

Where NMS keeps the best box of an overlapping group, `sv.box_weighted_box_fusion` replaces the group with one box whose coordinates are the confidence-weighted average. The fused score is the group's mean confidence, so revisit any confidence filter tuned for NMS. (#2455)

![Boxes from three models, NMS result and weighted box fusion result on the same photo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a719969-6612-4b48-a203-e22bb03ea036)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

# Columns: x1, y1, x2, y2, confidence, class_id.
predictions = np.array(
    [
        [10, 10, 50, 50, 0.9, 0],
        [12, 11, 52, 50, 0.6, 0],
        [100, 100, 140, 140, 0.8, 1],
    ],
    dtype=float,
)
sv.box_weighted_box_fusion(predictions, iou_threshold=0.5)
# array([[100. , 100. , 140. , 140. ,   0.8,   1. ],
#        [ 10.8,  10.4,  50.8,  50. ,   0.75,  0. ]])
```

### Key point annotators with color palettes

`sv.VertexAnnotator`, `sv.EdgeAnnotator` and `sv.VertexLabelAnnotator` accept a `sv.ColorPalette` and a `color_lookup`. The new `sv.ColorLookup.KEYPOINT` colors each point by its index in the skeleton, so a joint keeps its color across people. `sv.ColorLookup.TRACK` isn't supported for key points and is rejected. (#2343)

![The same skeletons drawn with one color and with one color per joint](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7281259c-5449-4d86-9bcc-99cf48bc482f)

```python
import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

scene = np.zeros((100, 100, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
key_points = sv.KeyPoints(
    xy=np.array([[[20, 20], [50, 30], [40, 80]]], dtype=np.float32),
    class_id=np.array([0]),
)
annotator = sv.VertexAnnotator(
    color=sv.ColorPalette.DEFAULT, color_lookup=sv.ColorLookup.KEYPOINT
)
annotated = annotator.annotate(scene.copy(), key_points)
```

## 🔄 Migration guide

No breaking changes. Every API removed in 0.32.0 was deprecated in 0.29.0 and scheduled for removal, and warned on use since, so code that runs warning-free on 0.31 needs no change. If you still use one:

**`sv.KeyPoints.confidence`**: pass and read `keypoint_confidence` instead.

```python
# before
key_points = sv.KeyPoints(xy=xy, confidence=scores)
scores = key_points.confidence

# after
key_points = sv.KeyPoints(xy=xy, keypoint_confidence=scores)
scores = key_points.keypoint_confidence
```

**Public `validate_*` helpers** (in `supervision.validators`, `supervision.annotators.utils`, `supervision.detection.core`, `supervision.detection.vlm` and `supervision.metrics.detection`, plus `sv.PercentageBarAnnotator.validate_custom_values`) have no public replacement. `sv.Detections` and `sv.KeyPoints` validate their own fields on construction.

```python
# before
from supervision.validators import validate_xyxy

validate_xyxy(xyxy)

# after: constructing the object validates it and raises ValueError on bad input
detections = sv.Detections(xyxy=xyxy)
```

**`merge_inner_detection_object_pair`, `merge_inner_detections_objects` and `merge_inner_detections_objects_without_iou`**: merge the detections and run `with_nmm` across classes. It needs `confidence`, which the old helpers did not. To fuse boxes from several models, use `sv.box_weighted_box_fusion`.

```python
# before
from supervision.detection.core import merge_inner_detections_objects

merged = merge_inner_detections_objects(single_object_detections, threshold=0.5)

# after
merged = sv.Detections.merge(single_object_detections).with_nmm(
    threshold=0.5, class_agnostic=True
)
```

Two edge-case behaviours also changed: `sv.JSONSink` raises on extra data that reuses a built-in detection field name, and `sv.xyxy_to_xywh` returns `int64` for integer input.

Three new deprecations will be removed in 0.35.0 at the earliest: a `list[sv.Color]` passed to `sv.VertexLabelAnnotator` (pass a `sv.ColorPalette` with `color_lookup=sv.ColorLookup.KEYPOINT` to keep one color per key point), `resolve_color`, `resolve_color_idx` and `get_color_by_index` (use a palette with `color_lookup`), and the default `mask_rasterizer` in `sv.DetectionDataset.from_coco`. Two re-exported import paths also warn until then: `load_coco_annotations` from `supervision.dataset.core` and `get_detection_size_category` from `supervision.metrics.mean_average_recall`; import them from `supervision.dataset.formats.coco` and `supervision.metrics.utils.object_size`.

## 📝 Notable changes

### 🚀 Added

- **Zone entry and exit counts** — `sv.PolygonZone` counts tracked objects entering and leaving, with per-class counts, `current_count_per_class`, `reset()`, and the new `minimum_crossing_threshold` and `max_absent_frames` options that smooth over boundary flicker and short occlusions. (#2770)
- **Zone dwell time** — `sv.PolygonZone.time_in_zone` reports seconds or frames inside per tracked object, and `trigger` takes an optional `timestamp`. (#2770)
- **Zone occupancy** — `sv.PolygonZone.occupancy_ratio` returns the fraction of the zone covered by masks, oriented boxes or boxes. (#1667)
- **Camera-mapped zone drawing** — `sv.PolygonZoneAnnotator.annotate` and `sv.LineZoneAnnotator.annotate` accept `coord_transform`. (#2760)
- **Semantic segmentation** — `sv.Detections.from_semantic_segmentation`, `from_inference` for Inference semantic results, and `from_ultralytics` for `task="semantic"` results. (#2898, #2915)
- **YOLO pose datasets** — `sv.KeyPointsDataset` with lazy loading, `split`, `merge`, `from_yolo` and `as_yolo`. (#2745)
- **Weighted Box Fusion** — `sv.box_weighted_box_fusion`. (#2455)
- **Class remapping** — `sv.Detections.remap_classes` renames, filters and re-indexes classes against a target list. (#1846, #2986)
- **Compact YOLO masks** — `sv.DetectionDataset.from_yolo(..., compact_masks=True)` keeps segmentation masks as `sv.CompactMask`. (#2834)
- **COCO mask rasterizer** — `sv.DetectionDataset.from_coco(..., mask_rasterizer=...)` and the new `supervision[coco]` extra for `pycocotools`. (#2714)
- **Key point annotator palettes** — `sv.ColorPalette` and `color_lookup` support, including `sv.ColorLookup.KEYPOINT`. (#2343)
- **Example video output** — the `time_in_zone` Ultralytics file example saves the annotated video with `--output_video_path`. (#1964)

### 🌱 Changed

- The `time_in_zone` examples now use `sv.PolygonZone.time_in_zone` instead of their own timers, so dwell restarts when an object leaves and returns. (#2770)
- Dataset merging builds a class-name lookup per dataset instead of rescanning the merged list. (#3017)
- `sv.CompactMask.area` sums runs in chunked NumPy reductions with `int64` accumulation, 3–9× faster in benchmarks for 100–500 masks. (#2744)

### 🗑️ Deprecated

- Passing a `list[sv.Color]` as `color` or `text_color` to `sv.VertexLabelAnnotator` is deprecated; pass a single `sv.Color`, or a `sv.ColorPalette` with `color_lookup=sv.ColorLookup.KEYPOINT` to keep one color per key point. Removed in 0.35.0. (#2343)
- `resolve_color`, `resolve_color_idx` and `get_color_by_index` in `supervision.annotators.utils` are deprecated and removed in 0.35.0. (#2343)
- Relying on the default `mask_rasterizer` in `sv.DetectionDataset.from_coco` for files with polygon segmentation now warns; the default changes to `"pycocotools"` no earlier than 0.35.0. (#2714)

### ❌ Removed

- The public `validate_*` helpers, deprecated since 0.29.0. Supervision uses private `_validate_*` helpers; `sv.Detections` and `sv.KeyPoints` validate on construction. (#3019)
- `merge_inner_detection_object_pair`, `merge_inner_detections_objects` and `merge_inner_detections_objects_without_iou`, deprecated since 0.29.0. Use `sv.Detections.merge(...).with_nmm(class_agnostic=True)`. (#3019)
- `sv.KeyPoints.confidence` and the `confidence` constructor argument, deprecated since 0.29.0. Use `keypoint_confidence`. (#3019)

### 🔧 Fixed

- `sv.metrics.MeanAverageRecall` no longer copies masks for every size range and no longer fails on metadata that cannot be deep-copied. (#2953)
- `sv.resize_image(keep_aspect_ratio=True)` and `sv.letterbox_image` no longer lose one pixel on the fitted axis. (#2952)
- `sv.xyxy_to_xywh` no longer wraps around on large integer boxes; integer input returns `int64`, or `float64` past the `int64` range. (#2951)
- `sv.JSONSink` now raises when extra data uses a built-in detection field name, instead of silently overwriting the field. (#2949)

## 🏆 Contributors

- **Piotr Skalski** (@SkalskiP, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/skalskip92/)) — added `ColorPalette` and `color_lookup` support to the key point annotators and deprecated the loose color-resolution helpers.
- **Rahul Sangamker** (@rs-03) — added `box_weighted_box_fusion` for Weighted Box Fusion.
- **Miral Amin** (@aminmiral, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/miral-a-976272283/)) — added `KeyPointsDataset` for YOLO pose datasets with lazy loading, split, merge and export.
- **Advait Shukla** (@AdvaitS) — added `PolygonZone` entry/exit counting, per-class counts and `time_in_zone` dwell time.
- **Archit H Barve** (@AHB102) — added `PolygonZone.occupancy_ratio`.
- **Aashish Anand** (@AshAnand34) — added `Detections.remap_classes`.
- **Christoph Deil** (@cdeil, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/christophdeil)) — added a `pycocotools` mask rasterizer option and the `coco` extra for `DetectionDataset.from_coco`.
- **Wentao Tong** (@tongwentao) — added compact mask loading to `DetectionDataset.from_yolo`.
- **NIKHIL** (@Nikhi00718, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nikhil-v-engineer)) — loaded Ultralytics semantic segmentation results in `Detections.from_ultralytics`.
- **Kari Pikkarainen** (@kari-pikkarainen, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/karipikkarainen/recent-activity/all/)) — added `coord_transform` to the polygon and line zone annotators.
- **A Aswanth Raj** (@aswanth-07, [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/a-aswanth-raj/)) — sped up `remap_classes` and dataset merging with class-name lookups.

name: Skill 4.10.0
body:
- **DESIGN.md as a map.** A long DESIGN.md reaches your agent as a short map of where tokens, components and layouts live, and the agent looks up one token, component or section when it needs it. `design-compact` proposes the map and writes it only when you agree.

- **Drift you can act on.** When the code contradicts DESIGN.md, Impeccable names what it contradicts.

- **Motion you can check.** `animate` captures the motion it built and reviews it from that evidence.

- **Finished world runs.** A world run ends with the site, walks its direction over the captures before the final review, and records DESIGN.md from what shipped.

- **Steadier Live.** The Live bar stays still under the pointer, and the missing PRODUCT.md notice shows once.

name: impeccable engine engine-v0.1.27
body: Prebuilt impeccable engine binaries (engine-v0.1.27). The launcher, the npm shim and impeccable install download these on first run. Docs: https://impeccable.style

name: CLI 4.10.0
body:
- **Your switches, in every agent.** The switches you turn on in Impeccable reach your agents' rule files within seconds. `switches-refresh --now` syncs them on the spot.

- **Page shots.** `shot` saves a page at desktop and phone widths.

- **Side tabs on rounded boxes.** The detector catches a bar down one side of a rounded box, whether it is a border, an inset shadow or a pseudo-element. A bar on a square box is fine and no longer flagged.

- **Every clone finds its repository.** Remotes through an SSH host alias, or spelled in another case, match the repository on GitHub.

- **Codex: trust Impeccable's hooks.** Codex runs a new or changed hook only after you trust it. When Codex says "Hooks need review", choose Trust all and continue, or trust Impeccable's hooks in `/hooks`. A later release will trust them for you when you connect.

name: Impeccable Loop 0.2.0
body: Answers in Loop now wake Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot CLI and opencode, as they already did Claude Code. An answer that lands while an agent is mid-turn, or after its session ended, still reaches it.

## What's Changed

Another release! This one isn't quite a big or heavy on the bugfixes as some of our other releases, but I wanted to get something out to you all anyway.

Most significantly, @ecairol did some amazing work enhancing how Harper ranks its spelling suggestions. You'll find that the suggestions in this version are for more correct _in context_ than ever before. Definitely a welcome improvement.
We also added the ability to load Weirpacks in the Desktop app, after several requests. In the Chrome Extension, you should see more relevant checks in more places.

# Cua Driver 0.54.0

## Summary

This release adds 1 features and includes 3 fixes.

## Features

- report is_password for Windows Edit elements. ([#8124](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/8124)) Thanks @WingedGuardian.

## Fixes

- exit the macOS daemon when an update replaces its app. ([#8135](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/8135)) reported by @gabrielhamalwa.
- fall back to WARP for unusable Windows captures. ([#8131](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/8131)) Thanks @SDSLeon.
- wait 40 ms after a foreground Windows desktop click and accept a hidden owned dialog. ([#8160](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/8160)) Thanks @CMGS.

## Contributors

Thanks to @CMGS, @gabrielhamalwa, @SDSLeon, @WingedGuardian for contributing to this release.

## Install

macOS and Linux:

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)"
```

Windows:

```powershell
irm https://cua.ai/driver/install.ps1 | iex
```

Cua Driver ships universal macOS binaries, x86_64 and arm64 Windows builds,
and Linux preview builds. Release assets also include tag-pinned installer and
uninstaller scripts.

## Why GitHub says “Pre-release”

GitHub's label is used only to keep this monorepo's repository-wide “Latest”
pointer from switching between independently released products. A plain Cua
Driver SemVer is a stable release; npm and PyPI publish it on
their normal stable channels, and the installers resolve the versioned
`cua-driver-rs-v*` releases directly.
